title: How Does a Jet Engine Work?
hook: Most of the air in this jet engine never touches the fire.

scenes.label: THE SECRET
scenes.line: Most of the air passing through this modern jet engine never even touches the fire.

scenes.label: THE GIANT FAN
scenes.line: First, a giant fan pulls air in. Much of it flows around the engine core.

scenes.label: SQUEEZE THE AIR
scenes.line: Inside the core, compressor stages squeeze the remaining air to a higher pressure.

scenes.label: CONTINUOUS FIRE
scenes.line: Fuel mixes with compressed air and burns continuously, making high energy gas.

scenes.label: POWER FROM GAS
scenes.line: The hot gas spins turbines connected by shafts to the compressor and the big fan.

scenes.label: THE THRUST
scenes.line: The fan and the core accelerate air backward. That change in momentum pushes the aircraft forward. Follow for more engineering.

title: How Do Giant Tunnel Boring Machines Work?
hook: This machine builds a tunnel as it digs.

scenes.label: A MOVING FACTORY
scenes.line: A tunnel boring machine does more than drill. It can build the tunnel as it moves.

scenes.label: CUTTERHEAD
scenes.line: Its rotating cutterhead presses hardened cutting tools into the ground ahead.

scenes.label: REMOVE THE SPOIL
scenes.line: Excavated material travels backward on conveyors or through a slurry pipeline, depending on the machine.

scenes.label: PUSH FORWARD
scenes.line: Hydraulic jacks press against the completed tunnel lining to move the machine forward.

scenes.label: BUILD THE WALL
scenes.line: In many soft ground machines, an erector places precast concrete segments into a protective ring.

scenes.label: REPEAT
scenes.line: Cut, remove, push, and install the next ring. The exact method depends on the geology. Follow for more engineering.

title: How Do Spacecraft Survive Reentry?
hook: A spacecraft survives reentry by managing extreme heat.

scenes.label: THE HOT RETURN
scenes.line: Returning from orbit, a spacecraft plows into increasingly dense air at enormous speed.

scenes.label: HOT GAS
scenes.line: Air compressed by the shock wave becomes extremely hot in front of the vehicle.

scenes.label: HEAT SHIELD
scenes.line: The heat shield keeps most of that heat away from the crew or sensitive equipment.

scenes.label: TWO STRATEGIES
scenes.line: Some shields deliberately shed material as they heat up. Others use reusable insulating tiles.

scenes.label: SLOW DOWN
scenes.line: Atmospheric drag takes away the spacecraft's kinetic energy and slows its descent.

scenes.label: SAFE DESCENT
scenes.line: Shield design depends on the vehicle and mission. It is not simply a layer of ordinary metal. Follow for more engineering.

title: How Do Submarines Control Their Depth?
hook: A submarine can change its buoyancy on purpose.

scenes.label: SINK ON PURPOSE
scenes.line: A submarine uses ballast tanks to change how much water it displaces relative to its weight.

scenes.label: FLOOD THE TANKS
scenes.line: To dive from the surface, seawater enters the main ballast tanks as air escapes.

scenes.label: TRIM THE BOAT
scenes.line: Smaller trim tanks help balance the submarine and adjust its buoyancy.

scenes.label: STEER UNDERWATER
scenes.line: While moving, diving planes generate hydrodynamic forces to control depth and angle.

scenes.label: COME BACK UP
scenes.line: Compressed air can force water out of the main ballast tanks to restore positive buoyancy.

scenes.label: A CONTROLLED BALANCE
scenes.line: Buoyancy, trim, speed, and control surfaces work together to manage a dive. Follow for more engineering.

title: How Do Tower Cranes Grow Taller?
hook: This crane can help build itself higher.

scenes.label: A SELF CLIMBING CRANE
scenes.line: Some tower cranes grow taller using a special hydraulic climbing frame.

scenes.label: MAKE ROOM
scenes.line: The climbing system temporarily lifts the upper crane assembly to make room below.

scenes.label: INSERT A SECTION
scenes.line: An additional mast section is moved into the opening using the crane or an assist mechanism.

scenes.label: SECURE THE JOINT
scenes.line: Crews align and securely connect the new section following the manufacturer's procedures.

scenes.label: CLIMB AGAIN
scenes.line: The climbing frame resets so the process can be repeated for another section.

scenes.label: STAY STABLE
scenes.line: Tall cranes may also need ties to the building, according to their engineered design. Follow for more engineering.

title: How Do Flight Recorders Survive Crashes?
hook: An aircraft black box is built to protect its memory.

scenes.label: NOT ACTUALLY BLACK
scenes.line: Flight recorders are usually bright orange so investigators can find them more easily.

scenes.label: SAVE THE DATA
scenes.line: Crash protected memory stores flight data or cockpit audio, depending on the recorder.

scenes.label: IMPACT PROTECTION
scenes.line: A tough protective enclosure helps the memory survive severe impact loads.

scenes.label: FIRE AND HEAT
scenes.line: Thermal insulation and protective materials help it withstand extreme heat for specified periods.

scenes.label: UNDERWATER
scenes.line: A fitted underwater locator beacon emits acoustic pings after it is activated by water.

scenes.label: FIND THE ANSWERS
scenes.line: Protection improves the chance of recovering crucial evidence, but no device is indestructible. Follow for more engineering.
